description: We’re xSplesh, a team of two friends from Yakutsk. We’re interested in technology and enjoy learning by trying things out ourselves. We joined NASA Space Apps to see how far we could take an idea together in one weekend
summary:
On June 15, 2024, MODIS recorded 7 hot-spot detections in our study area in Central Yakutia. VIIRS recorded 31. Where did their observations overlap? On the xSplesh map, the detections fell into four grid cells, and both instruments reported hot spots in only one of them.

xSplesh turns NASA FIRMS data into an interactive calendar and chart of daily detections from 2020 to 2024. For June 2024, an animated map groups MODIS and VIIRS observations into the same 0.1° grid. Press Play to see, day by day, which areas were flagged by both instruments and which were flagged by just one. This gives users a way to compare where the instruments detected activity, even when their raw counts differ.
details:
We built xSplesh to make MODIS and VIIRS fire detections easier to compare in Central Yakutia. The calendar and chart show daily detections from each instrument from 2020 to 2024. On the June 2024 map, users can choose a date or press Play to watch the pattern change day by day.

We used Python to process NASA FIRMS CSV files and export the results as JSON. To compare the instruments on the map, we grouped detections by UTC date and placed them on a common 0.1° grid. Each cell shows whether MODIS, VIIRS, or both recorded a hot spot there that day. For example, on June 25, both instruments recorded detections in 29 of the 42 cells with detections.

This approach makes it easier to see where observations overlap despite differences in spatial resolution and overpass times. An overlap means detections occurred in the same grid cell on the same UTC date. A cell may contain multiple detections, so cell counts should be interpreted as areas with recorded activity.

We built the interface with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, used Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for the interactive map, and hosted the app on GitHub Pages.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS Archive — MODIS C6.1 and Suomi NPP VIIRS C2 active fire detections
